observations: The slice was named rather than chosen, so the run is evidence about content and none about routing. The report said so unprompted.

Reading a card's variant summary rather than its body nearly cleared a defect a second time: an assertion variant permitting a compiled-out check was read as permitting a weaker contract, and the obligation attached to that variant - write the contract precisely enough that a caller can tell whether they satisfy it - was the thing the code failed.

An option list of three enforcement mechanisms was run to completion and one was chosen, when the correct answer was that none applied because the validation boundary the list presupposes did not exist in that code.

A compilation-context rule was judged violated from a view of the benchmark file alone; reading the definition of the code under test reversed the answer, because the production build inlines it exactly as the fixture does.

Of five reported guidance defects, three survived verification against the card. One was a routing failure whose card already covered the case, and one was a form preference the card's rule already admitted.
Pass two produced 11 techniques owned by existing cards against 6 with no owner, on a slice deliberately aimed at regions the first run left cold.

One gap candidate recorded after the first run - a compiled-out feature expressed as no-op implementations of the same interface - was independently rediscovered, but in the same codebase and the same project's house style, so it remains one sample rather than two.
